summary: Evidence supports conditional context management, not a universal preference for less context. Recent coding-agent work finds semantic-use limits, strong tool-mediated navigation, and the largest compaction gains when a window would otherwise overflow.

items.text: Lost in the Middle: How Language Models Use Long Contexts — Nelson F. Liu et al. (2024). TACL experiments found performance often highest when relevant information appears at the beginning or end and degraded when it appears in the middle, even for models marketed with long context windows. This directly undermines the assumption that dumping more context is harmless.

LLMLingua: Compressing Prompts for Accelerated Inference of Large Language Models — Huiqiang Jiang et al. (2023). EMNLP experiments report up to 20-times prompt compression with limited performance loss across four evaluated settings. This is direct compression evidence, but results depend on task, compressor, and downstream model.

LongLLMLingua: Accelerating and Enhancing LLMs in Long Context Scenarios via Prompt Compression — Huiqiang Jiang et al. (2024). ACL experiments use question-aware compression and document reordering to improve selected long-context tasks while reducing cost and latency. It supports relevance-oriented compaction, not unconstrained summarization of decisions.

Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Knowledge-Intensive NLP Tasks — Patrick Lewis et al. (2020). NeurIPS experiments show that retrieving external passages can improve several knowledge-intensive tasks and preserve provenance opportunities. This is adjacent evidence for just-in-time retrieval; repositories, code relations, and evolving work state were not studied.

Štorek et al., ACL 2026: ten models retrieved code nearly perfectly while semantic reasoning over code placed in the middle of 4k–16k-token synthetic contexts could degrade sharply. This isolates one failure mode, not the effect of compaction in a full coding-agent workflow.

Cao et al., 2026 preprint: off-the-shelf coding agents used filesystem tools and scripts to process very large text corpora, and extra retrievers did not consistently improve results. The tasks were mainly long-text processing, not code editing.

Fan et al., September 2026 preprint: across four models and two coding benchmarks, context management helped most at tighter window budgets by preventing overflow; its average success advantage shrank as budgets grew from 32k to 128k. The findings are bound to the tested harness policies.
